Ticket: REQ0039182

Status: Resolved
Requester: Elena Rostova <mock-elena.rostova@synthetic-test.local>
Phone: +1-555-0188
Department: Finance Operations
Device: LAPTOP-NYC-4029.synthetic-test.local
Device ID: 00000000-0000-4000-a000-000000000042
OS: Windows 11 Enterprise 22H2
Assigned Tech: mock-tech-sam@synthetic-test.local

DESCRIPTION OF PROBLEM:
User reported that following a prompt from Dell Command Update to reboot for a system firmware update, the laptop restarted directly into a blue screen displaying:
"BitLocker - Enter the recovery key for this drive"
The user does not have the 48-digit numerical recovery password and is locked out of the operating system.

TECHNICAL NOTES & RESOLUTION:
1. Contacted user by telephone to verify identity following Corporate IT Security Verification Procedure (verified employee ID #49201 and manager confirmation).
2. Accessed Microsoft Entra admin center (https://entra.microsoft.com) > Devices > All Devices.
   Located device LAPTOP-NYC-4029 by Object ID 00000000-0000-4000-a000-000000000042.
   Retrieved BitLocker Key ID 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555 and 48-digit Recovery Key:
   123456-789012-345678-901234-567890-123456-789012-345678
3. Read recovery key to user over verified phone line. User entered recovery key and Windows successfully loaded desktop.
4. Investigated root cause of BitLocker trip:
   Checked Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > BitLocker-API > Management.
   Found Event ID 834: "BitLocker determined that the TCG log is invalid for TPM 2.0 PCR[7] binding."
   The Dell BIOS update from version 1.14.0 to 1.18.1 modified the UEFI Secure Boot PCR 7 hash table without temporarily suspending BitLocker protection.
5. Remediated PCR binding drift to prevent BitLocker prompt on subsequent reboots:
   Opened Administrator PowerShell console and executed:
   Suspend-BitLocker -MountPoint "C:" -RebootCount 1
   Restart-Computer
6. Following reboot, BitLocker automatically resumed encryption and sealed the TPM with the new firmware measurements.
7. Executed verification command:
   Get-BitLockerVolume -MountPoint "C:" | Select-Object MountPoint, VolumeStatus, ProtectionStatus, KeyProtector
   ProtectionStatus returned 'On' with 'Tpm' and 'RecoveryPassword' protectors active.
8. Initiated second test reboot. Laptop booted directly to Windows login screen without prompting for recovery key.
